common_name: Black Peony Poppy (Dark Maroon-Black Double Breadseed Poppy)

planting.note: Surface sow in early spring or fall; needs light and cool soil to germinate.

directions: Scatter the tiny seed on the soil surface in early spring or fall, leaving it uncovered since light and cool temperatures aid germination; grow in full sun in well-drained soil, where it is drought tolerant once established. Black Peony bears huge, fully double blooms in the darkest maroon-black of any commonly grown poppy, the ruffled, densely packed petals giving each flower the lush, rounded fullness of a peony rather than the simple cupped form of a wild poppy. Direct sow only, since poppies resent root disturbance, and let plants self-sow for future years once established. The seed pods that follow the blooms are attractive dried for arrangements, and all parts of the plant are toxic if ingested.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun; Oriental poppies resent wet, heavy soil and summer humidity, so good drainage is essential. Like other Oriental poppies it flowers in late spring, then dies back to dormancy through summer heat before re-emerging with fresh foliage in fall, so mark its location to avoid disturbing the dormant crown during the summer gap. It performs best in climates with cooler summers and struggles in the humid, hot conditions of the Deep South.
